frequency_question: How often do high-conviction regulatory interventions with substantial cost increases get carried through to final publication by motivated principals within a similar timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes major agency rulemakings explicitly championed by executive principals that impose massive cost multipliers on established economic systems. Excludes routine adjustments, minor guidance, and measures abandoned due to internal principal disinterest.
window: First 24 months of an administration, evaluated over a rolling 300-day implementation window
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named; representative of high-will, high-disruption executive actions carried to final rule stages.
known_gaps: Excludes minor regulatory adjustments that lacked principal-level prioritization.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to presidential administration lifecycle and internal executive branch rulemaking dynamics.
